stimuli.text: Researchers collected data from 450 adults. For each one, they recorded optimism score and the number of days of illness in a year. The correlation between the two measures was r = −0.30.

Researchers investigated whether the wording of a question changes what witnesses remember. They recruited 100 adult volunteers who watched a film of a car accident and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition were asked how fast the cars were going when they smashed into each other. Participants in the other condition were asked how fast the cars were going when they contacted each other. The researchers then recorded the speed in kilometers per hour that each participant wrote down.

Researchers investigated whether children imitate aggressive behavior that they observe. They recruited 72 preschool children and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Children in one condition watched a video of an adult hitting an inflatable doll. Children in the other condition watched a video of an adult playing quietly with other toys. The researchers then recorded the number of times that each child hit the doll during ten minutes of free play.

Researchers collected data from 300 families. For each one, they recorded the warmth of parenting, as rated by observers and the child's self-esteem score. The correlation between the two measures was r = +0.48.

Researchers collected data from 1,000 students. For each one, they recorded intelligence test score at age 11 and average school grade at age 16. The correlation between the two measures was r = +0.60.
Researchers collected data from 250 adults. For each one, they recorded resting heart rate and self-rated anxiety. The correlation between the two measures was r = +0.38.

Researchers investigated whether the presence of other people slows the reporting of an emergency. They recruited 80 university students and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition were filling in a form in a room with four other people when smoke began to enter the room. Participants in the other condition were filling in the form alone when smoke began to enter the room. The researchers then recorded the time in seconds before each participant left the room to report the smoke.

Researchers investigated whether an expected reward reduces children's later interest in drawing. They recruited 60 preschool children who enjoyed drawing and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Children in one condition were promised a certificate for drawing and received it. Children in the other condition drew with no reward mentioned. The researchers then recorded the number of minutes that each child chose to spend drawing during free time one week later.

Researchers investigated whether regular aerobic exercise improves memory in older adults. They recruited 100 adults aged 60 to 75 and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition walked briskly for 40 minutes three times a week for six months. Participants in the other condition did gentle stretching for the same amount of time. The researchers then recorded the number of locations that each participant correctly recalled on a spatial memory test.

Researchers collected data from 1,200 teenagers. For each one, they recorded the number of hours of social media use per day and score on a depression questionnaire. The correlation between the two measures was r = +0.28.

Researchers investigated whether practice quizzes improve memory more than rereading. They recruited 120 university students and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition read a passage once and then took three practice quizzes on it. Participants in the other condition read the same passage four times. The researchers then recorded the percentage of questions that each participant answered correctly on a test one week later.

Researchers investigated whether cognitive-behavioral therapy reduces depression. They recruited 90 adults diagnosed with major depressive disorder and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition received twelve weekly sessions of cognitive-behavioral therapy. Participants in the other condition were placed on a waiting list for twelve weeks and were treated afterward. The researchers then recorded each participant's score on a standard depression questionnaire after twelve weeks.

Researchers investigated whether a smiling expression makes cartoons seem funnier. They recruited 90 university students and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition held a pen between their teeth, which produces a smile. Participants in the other condition held a pen between their lips, which prevents a smile. The researchers then recorded the rating from 1 to 10 that each participant gave to a set of cartoons.

Read the summary of a hypothetical study, then answer parts A to F.

**Introduction.** Researchers investigated whether a phone conversation reduces what drivers notice. They hypothesized that phone use would affect attention to the road.

**Participants.** The sample was 64 licensed drivers, recruited from one city. All participants gave informed consent, were told they could withdraw at any time, and were debriefed afterward. The plan was approved by an institutional review board.

**Method.** The participants were randomly assigned to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition held a hands-free phone conversation while using a driving simulator. Participants in the other condition used the driving simulator without a phone. The researchers recorded the number of road signs out of 30 that each participant failed to notice.

**Results.** The group that talked on the phone: mean road signs missed (out of 30) = 11.4. The group that drove without a phone: mean road signs missed (out of 30) = 4.9. The difference was statistically significant (p = 0.01).

Use the three hypothetical sources to answer the question: **Does sleep improve memory?**

**Source A.** In an experiment, 60 students learned a list of word pairs at 9 p.m. Half were randomly assigned to sleep normally and half to stay awake all night. Twelve hours later, the sleep group recalled a mean of 31 pairs out of 40 and the awake group recalled a mean of 22 (p = 0.01).

**Source B.** Researchers recorded the brain activity of 25 adults in a sleep laboratory after they had learned a maze. The more slow-wave (NREM stage 3) sleep a participant had, the faster that participant completed the maze the next morning (r = +0.55).

**Source C.** A survey of 900 high school students found that those who reported sleeping fewer than six hours on school nights had lower average grades than those who slept eight hours or more. The researchers noted that students who slept less also reported more stress and more hours of paid work.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the deep sleep stage marked by slow delta waves, in which a person is hard to wake?

options.why: REM sleep is the sleep stage with rapid eye movements, vivid dreams, an active brain and relaxed muscles.
Correct. NREM stage 3 is the deep sleep stage marked by slow delta waves, in which a person is hard to wake.
The circadian rhythm is the body's roughly 24-hour cycle of wakefulness and sleep.
NREM stage 1 is the brief, light first stage of sleep, in which a person may have hypnagogic sensations such as falling.

questions.explanation: NREM stage 3 is the deep sleep stage marked by slow delta waves, in which a person is hard to wake.

questions.stem: Participants are told a study is about memory when it is really about obedience. Which research practice is this?

options.why: An institutional review board is the committee that reviews research plans to make sure participants are treated ethically.
Informed consent is the agreement of participants to take part after they have been told what a study involves.
Correct. Deception is the misleading of participants about the true purpose of a study, allowed only when necessary and followed by debriefing.
Debriefing is the explaining of a study's purpose, and any deception, to participants after it ends.

questions.explanation: Deception is the misleading of participants about the true purpose of a study, allowed only when necessary and followed by debriefing.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes procedural memory?

options.text: The memory to carry out a planned action in the future
options.why: That describes prospective memory.

options.text: The implicit memory of how to perform skills and actions
options.why: Correct. This is what procedural memory means.

options.text: The explicit memory of facts and general knowledge
options.why: That describes semantic memory.

options.text: The explicit memory of personally experienced events
options.why: That describes episodic memory.

questions.explanation: Procedural memory is the implicit memory of how to perform skills and actions.

questions.stem: After being bitten by a large brown dog, Eva is afraid of all dogs. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: Higher-order conditioning is the pairing of a new neutral stimulus with an existing conditioned stimulus to create a second conditioned stimulus.
Acquisition is in classical conditioning, the first stage, in which the neutral stimulus is paired with the unconditioned stimulus and the response is learned.
Stimulus discrimination is the learned ability to respond to the conditioned stimulus but not to similar stimuli.
Correct. Stimulus generalization is the tendency to respond to stimuli that are similar to the conditioned stimulus.

questions.explanation: Stimulus generalization is the tendency to respond to stimuli that are similar to the conditioned stimulus.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes assimilation?

options.text: A mental grouping of similar objects, events, ideas or people
options.why: That describes a concept.

options.text: The best or most typical example of a category
options.why: That describes a prototype.

options.text: A mental framework that organizes and interprets information
options.why: That describes a schema.

options.text: The interpretation of a new experience in terms of an existing schema
options.why: Correct. This is what assimilation means.

questions.explanation: Assimilation is the interpretation of a new experience in terms of an existing schema.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes an eclectic approach?

options.text: The use of techniques from several types of therapy, depending on the client's problem
options.why: Correct. This is what an eclectic approach means.

options.text: The presence of two or more disorders in the same person at the same time
options.why: That describes comorbidity.

options.text: The view that disorders result from the interaction of biological, psychological and social factors
options.why: That describes the biopsychosocial model.

options.text: The view that a disorder develops when an inherited vulnerability is triggered by stressful experience
options.why: That describes the diathesis-stress model.

questions.explanation: An eclectic approach is the use of techniques from several types of therapy, depending on the client's problem.

questions.stem: A twenty-five-year-old focuses on forming a committed, loving relationship. Which of Erikson's stages is this?

options.why: Identity versus role confusion is Erikson's stage in adolescence, in which teenagers work out who they are.
Integrity versus despair is Erikson's stage in late adulthood, in which people look back on life with satisfaction or regret.
Generativity versus stagnation is Erikson's stage in middle adulthood, in which people seek to contribute to the world through family and work.
Correct. Intimacy versus isolation is Erikson's stage in young adulthood, in which people seek close, lasting relationships.

questions.explanation: Intimacy versus isolation is Erikson's stage in young adulthood, in which people seek close, lasting relationships.

questions.stem: A school celebrates the languages, foods and holidays of all the cultures among its students. Which view does this reflect?

options.why: A superordinate goal is a shared goal that can be reached only if groups cooperate, which reduces conflict between them.
Obedience is the following of the direct commands of an authority figure.
A social trap is a situation in which people who each pursue their own interest end up harming everyone.
Correct. Multiculturalism is the view that the different cultural groups in a society should be valued and should keep their identities.

questions.explanation: Multiculturalism is the view that the different cultural groups in a society should be valued and should keep their identities.

questions.stem: Students catch more colds during exam weeks than at other times of year. Which effect of stress best explains this?

options.why: Problem-focused coping is the reducing of stress by changing the stressor itself or the way one deals with it.
Emotion-focused coping is the reducing of stress by managing one's emotional reaction rather than the stressor.
Hypertension is persistently high blood pressure, which is made more likely by chronic stress.
Correct. Immune suppression is the weakening of the body's defenses against illness during long-term stress.

questions.explanation: Immune suppression is the weakening of the body's defenses against illness during long-term stress.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes the sunk-cost fallacy?

options.text: The tendency to keep investing in something because of what has already been spent on it
options.why: Correct. This is what the sunk-cost fallacy means.

options.text: The activation, often without awareness, of certain associations that then influence perception or behavior
options.why: That describes priming.

options.text: The way the wording of an issue affects decisions and judgments
options.why: That describes framing.

options.text: The mistaken belief that a random event is more likely because it has not happened recently
options.why: That describes the gambler's fallacy.

questions.explanation: The sunk-cost fallacy is the tendency to keep investing in something because of what has already been spent on it.

questions.stem: In one culture, people are expected to hide their disappointment in public; in another, they show it openly. This difference reflects which of the following?

options.why: The facial-feedback hypothesis is the idea that the expression on a person's face can influence the emotion the person feels.
Correct. A display rule is a cultural rule about which emotions may be shown, when and to whom.
The broaden-and-build theory is the theory that positive emotions widen a person's awareness and help build lasting skills and resources.
An elicitor is an event or stimulus that triggers an emotion.

questions.explanation: A display rule is a cultural rule about which emotions may be shown, when and to whom.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes an fMRI?

options.text: The destruction of a small area of brain tissue to study its function
options.why: That describes lesioning.

options.text: The condition in which the two hemispheres cannot communicate because the corpus callosum has been cut
options.why: That describes a split brain.

options.text: A scan that shows brain activity by tracking blood flow
options.why: Correct. This is what an fMRI means.

options.text: An in-depth study of one individual, such as a patient with unusual brain damage
options.why: That describes a case study.

questions.explanation: An fMRI is a scan that shows brain activity by tracking blood flow.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes overgeneralization?

options.text: The applying of a grammar rule too widely, as in 'goed' or 'mouses'
options.why: Correct. This is what overgeneralization means.

options.text: The vowel-like sounds, such as 'ooh', that infants make from about two months
options.why: That describes cooing.

options.text: The stage from about four months in which infants produce many consonant-vowel sounds, such as 'ba-ba'
options.why: That describes babbling.

options.text: The stage from about age 1 in which a child speaks mostly in single words
options.why: That describes the one-word stage.

questions.explanation: Overgeneralization is the applying of a grammar rule too widely, as in 'goed' or 'mouses'.

questions.stem: After failing a quiz, Ana says, 'I need a better strategy and more practice,' and works harder. Which belief does this show?

options.why: An achievement test is a test that measures what a person has already learned.
Stereotype threat is the worry about confirming a negative stereotype about one's group, which can lower performance.
An aptitude test is a test that predicts a person's ability to learn or perform in the future.
Correct. A growth mindset is the belief that intelligence can be developed through effort and learning.

questions.explanation: A growth mindset is the belief that intelligence can be developed through effort and learning.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a possible third variable that could explain the correlation?

options.text: The number of days of illness in a year
options.why: This is one of the two variables that were measured.
This is the statistic, not a variable.
Correct. A third variable could influence both measures and so produce the correlation.
This is one of the two variables that were measured.

questions.explanation: A third variable could influence both measures and so produce the correlation.

questions.stem: Which group served as the control group?

options.why: Only the comparison group is the control group.

options.text: The group asked the question with the word 'smashed'
options.why: This group received the treatment being tested: it is the experimental group.

options.text: The group asked the question with the word 'contacted'
options.why: Correct. The control group is the comparison group that does not receive the treatment being tested.

options.text: Neither group, because the study had no comparison condition
options.why: The second condition is the comparison.

questions.explanation: The control group is the comparison group that does not receive the treatment being tested.

questions.stem: Seven students took a memory test. Their scores were 9, 7, 4, 15, 7, 11, 3. What is the mean of the scores?

options.why: That is the median.
Correct. Add the scores (56) and divide by 7.
That is the range.
That is the highest score.

questions.explanation: In order, the scores are 3, 4, 7, 7, 9, 11, 15. Add the scores (56) and divide by 7. The one very high score pulls the mean (8) above the median (7), so the distribution is positively skewed.

questions.stem: Which brain structure stores the well-practiced skill of riding a bicycle?

options.why: The thalamus is the brain's sensory relay station, which directs incoming signals to the cortex.
The reticular activating system is the network of neurons in the brainstem that controls arousal and alertness.
The pituitary gland is the master gland of the endocrine system, which is controlled by the hypothalamus.
Correct. The cerebellum is the structure at the back of the brainstem that coordinates balance, movement and procedural learning.

questions.explanation: The cerebellum is the structure at the back of the brainstem that coordinates balance, movement and procedural learning.

questions.stem: Although she dislikes the film, Ida says she loved it because all her friends did and she wants to fit in. Which kind of influence is this?

options.why: Informational social influence is the influence that comes from a person's willingness to accept others' views as evidence about reality.
Correct. Normative social influence is the influence that comes from a person's desire to gain approval or avoid rejection.
The peripheral route to persuasion is persuasion that works through surface cues, such as an attractive or famous speaker.
The foot-in-the-door technique is the strategy of getting agreement to a small request first so that a larger request is more likely to be accepted.

questions.explanation: Normative social influence is the influence that comes from a person's desire to gain approval or avoid rejection.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the neurodevelopmental disorder marked by inattention, hyperactivity and impulsiveness?

options.why: A specific learning disorder is the neurodevelopmental disorder marked by persistent difficulty in reading, writing or math despite normal intelligence.
Correct. Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder is the neurodevelopmental disorder marked by inattention, hyperactivity and impulsiveness.
Autism spectrum disorder is the neurodevelopmental disorder marked by difficulties with social communication and by repetitive behaviors or narrow interests.
Anorexia nervosa is the eating disorder in which a person restricts food to the point of being dangerously underweight, with an intense fear of gaining weight.

questions.explanation: Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder is the neurodevelopmental disorder marked by inattention, hyperactivity and impulsiveness.

questions.stem: Many antidepressant drugs work by raising the level of one neurotransmitter that regulates mood. Which neurotransmitter is this?

options.why: Acetylcholine is the neurotransmitter that enables muscle movement, learning and memory.
Norepinephrine is the neurotransmitter that helps control alertness and arousal.
Substance P is the neurotransmitter that carries pain messages to the brain.
Correct. Serotonin is the neurotransmitter that affects mood, hunger and sleep.

questions.explanation: Serotonin is the neurotransmitter that affects mood, hunger and sleep.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the disorder in which a person has an intense, irrational fear of a particular object or situation?

options.why: Correct. A specific phobia is the disorder in which a person has an intense, irrational fear of a particular object or situation.
Social anxiety disorder is the disorder in which a person has an intense fear of being judged or embarrassed in social situations.
Agoraphobia is the disorder in which a person fears and avoids public places from which escape might be difficult.
Taijin kyofusho is the culture-bound anxiety syndrome, found mainly in Japan, marked by fear of offending or embarrassing others.

questions.explanation: A specific phobia is the disorder in which a person has an intense, irrational fear of a particular object or situation.

questions.stem: In the strange situation, a toddler explores happily while his mother is present, cries when she leaves and calms quickly when she returns. Which attachment style is this?

options.why: Disorganized attachment is the insecure attachment style in which a child shows confused, contradictory behavior toward the caregiver.
Correct. Secure attachment is the attachment style in which a child uses the caregiver as a safe base, is upset when the caregiver leaves and is comforted on return.
Avoidant attachment is the insecure attachment style in which a child seems indifferent when the caregiver leaves and ignores the caregiver on return.
Contact comfort is the comfort from physical touch that Harlow showed is more important to attachment than feeding.

questions.explanation: Secure attachment is the attachment style in which a child uses the caregiver as a safe base, is upset when the caregiver leaves and is comforted on return.

questions.stem: The moment Lia hears that her company is closing, her heart races and adrenaline surges. Which phase of the general adaptation syndrome is this?

options.why: Correct. The alarm reaction is the first phase of the general adaptation syndrome, in which the sympathetic nervous system is suddenly activated.
The resistance phase is the second phase of the general adaptation syndrome, in which the body stays highly aroused to cope with a continuing stressor.
The exhaustion phase is the third phase of the general adaptation syndrome, in which the body's resources run out and illness becomes more likely.
The general adaptation syndrome is Selye's three-phase description of the body's response to long-term stress: alarm, resistance and exhaustion.

questions.explanation: The alarm reaction is the first phase of the general adaptation syndrome, in which the sympathetic nervous system is suddenly activated.

questions.stem: Hugo knows the actor's name and can even say its first letter, but he cannot quite produce it. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: Correct. The tip-of-the-tongue phenomenon is the temporary inability to retrieve a word that one is sure one knows.
Repression is in psychodynamic theory, the pushing of anxiety-arousing memories out of awareness.
Proactive interference is the disruption of new learning by older memories.
The forgetting curve is the pattern in which memory fades quickly at first and then levels off.

questions.explanation: The tip-of-the-tongue phenomenon is the temporary inability to retrieve a word that one is sure one knows.

questions.stem: What is the dependent variable in this study?

options.why: Correct. The dependent variable is the outcome that the researchers measured.

options.text: The condition to which each one was assigned
options.why: This describes the independent variable.
A hypothesis is a prediction, not a variable.

options.text: The behavior of an adult model
options.why: This was manipulated by the researchers: it is the independent variable.

questions.explanation: The dependent variable is the outcome that the researchers measured.

questions.stem: A previously healthy student suddenly develops hallucinations after a period of intense stress and later recovers well. Which pattern of onset is this?

options.why: A positive symptom is a symptom of schizophrenia that adds an inappropriate behavior or experience, such as hallucinations.
Correct. An acute onset is the sudden appearance of schizophrenia, often after stress, from which recovery is more likely.
The dopamine hypothesis is the idea that schizophrenia involves excessive activity of the neurotransmitter dopamine.
A negative symptom is a symptom of schizophrenia that takes away a normal behavior, such as emotional expression or motivation.

questions.explanation: An acute onset is the sudden appearance of schizophrenia, often after stress, from which recovery is more likely.

questions.stem: Marc reads the assigned novel only because he wants a good grade. Which kind of motivation is this?

options.why: An approach-approach conflict is a conflict in which a person must choose between two attractive options.
Intrinsic motivation is the desire to do something for its own sake, because it is enjoyable or satisfying.
An avoidance-avoidance conflict is a conflict in which a person must choose between two unattractive options.
Correct. Extrinsic motivation is the desire to do something to gain a reward or avoid a punishment.

questions.explanation: Extrinsic motivation is the desire to do something to gain a reward or avoid a punishment.

questions.stem: Without knowing any of them, Mr. Hill feels dislike and distrust toward people from a neighboring town. This feeling is an example of which of the following?

options.why: Correct. Prejudice is an unjustified negative attitude toward a group and its members.
The just-world phenomenon is the tendency to believe that people get what they deserve.
A stereotype is a generalized belief about a group of people.
An implicit attitude is an attitude that a person holds without being aware of it.

questions.explanation: Prejudice is an unjustified negative attitude toward a group and its members.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes health psychology?

options.text: The response to stress in which the sympathetic nervous system prepares the body to attack or escape
options.why: That describes the fight-or-flight response.

options.text: The negative stress that harms well-being and performance
options.why: That describes distress.

options.text: The field that studies how behavior, thoughts and emotions affect physical health and illness
options.why: Correct. This is what health psychology means.

options.text: The positive, motivating stress that comes from a challenge
options.why: That describes eustress.

questions.explanation: Health psychology is the field that studies how behavior, thoughts and emotions affect physical health and illness.

questions.stem: Four studies of child development report these correlation coefficients: +0.61, −0.86, +0.52, +0.35. Which coefficient shows the weakest relationship?

options.why: +0.61 is farther from zero.
Correct. Strength is the distance from zero, whatever the sign; +0.35 is closest to zero.
+0.52 is farther from zero.
−0.86 is farther from zero.

questions.explanation: The sign of a correlation shows its direction; its distance from zero shows its strength. +0.35 is closest to zero.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as Erikson's stage in toddlerhood, in which children learn to do things for themselves?

options.why: Initiative versus guilt is Erikson's stage in the preschool years, in which children learn to start tasks and carry out plans.
Industry versus inferiority is Erikson's stage in elementary school, in which children learn to feel competent or else feel inadequate.
Trust versus mistrust is Erikson's stage in infancy, in which babies learn whether their needs will be met.
Correct. Autonomy versus shame and doubt is Erikson's stage in toddlerhood, in which children learn to do things for themselves.

questions.explanation: Autonomy versus shame and doubt is Erikson's stage in toddlerhood, in which children learn to do things for themselves.

questions.stem: If the data were shown on a scatterplot, what pattern would the points form?

options.why: Only a correlation of +1.00 or −1.00 gives a perfect line.

options.text: A shapeless cloud with no slope
options.why: That would show a correlation near zero.

options.text: A loose band that slopes upward from left to right
options.why: Correct. A moderate positive correlation appears as a band of points sloping upward.

options.text: A loose band that slopes downward from left to right
options.why: That would show a negative correlation.

questions.explanation: A moderate positive correlation appears as a band of points sloping upward.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the possibility that an unmeasured factor causes the relationship between two correlated variables?

options.why: A scatterplot is a graph in which each point shows one individual's values on two variables.
A negative correlation is a relationship in which one variable rises as the other falls.
Correct. The third variable problem is the possibility that an unmeasured factor causes the relationship between two correlated variables.
A positive correlation is a relationship in which two variables rise and fall together.

questions.explanation: The third variable problem is the possibility that an unmeasured factor causes the relationship between two correlated variables.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes an algorithm?

options.text: The tendency to approach a problem in a way that has worked before, even when it no longer works
options.why: That describes a mental set.

options.text: A step-by-step procedure that guarantees a solution
options.why: Correct. This is what an algorithm means.

options.text: The inability to see that an object can be used for something other than its usual purpose
options.why: That describes functional fixedness.

options.text: A simple thinking shortcut that is fast but can lead to errors
options.why: That describes a heuristic.

questions.explanation: An algorithm is a step-by-step procedure that guarantees a solution.

questions.stem: A second study of a different pair of measures finds r = −0.80. Which relationship is stronger?

options.text: Neither, because relationships with different signs cannot be compared
options.why: Strength can be compared by distance from zero.

options.text: The relationship with the positive sign, whatever its size
options.why: The sign shows direction, not strength.

options.text: The relationship in the second study, because its coefficient is farther from zero
options.why: Correct. The strength of a correlation is its distance from zero, whatever the sign.

options.text: The relationship in the first study, because its coefficient is closer to zero
options.why: A coefficient closer to zero shows a weaker relationship.

questions.explanation: The strength of a correlation is its distance from zero, whatever the sign.

questions.stem: Hearing a song from her school days brings back a flood of memories for Tina. The song is acting as which of the following?

options.why: Context-dependent memory is the improved recall that occurs in the same place where the information was learned.
The testing effect is the finding that practicing retrieval improves memory more than rereading.
Correct. A retrieval cue is a stimulus that helps bring a memory to mind.
State-dependent memory is the improved recall that occurs in the same physical state as when the information was learned.

questions.explanation: A retrieval cue is a stimulus that helps bring a memory to mind.

questions.stem: Which statement describes the directionality problem in this study?

options.text: It is unclear whether the first measure influences the second or the second influences the first
options.why: Correct. A correlation cannot show which variable, if either, comes first.

options.text: It is unclear whether the correlation is positive or negative
options.why: The sign of r shows the direction of the relationship.

options.text: It is unclear whether the two measures were recorded
options.why: Both measures were recorded.

options.text: It is unclear how many people took part
options.why: The sample size is stated.

questions.explanation: A correlation cannot show which variable, if either, comes first.

questions.stem: A blow to the very back of the head makes a person see flashes of light. Which lobes were affected?

options.why: Correct. The occipital lobes is the lobes at the back of the head, which process visual information.
The parietal lobes is the lobes at the top of the head, which process touch and spatial information.
The prefrontal cortex is the front part of the frontal lobes, which handles executive functions such as planning and self-control.
The frontal lobes is the lobes behind the forehead, which handle planning, judgment and voluntary movement.

questions.explanation: The occipital lobes is the lobes at the back of the head, which process visual information.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as a person's overall feeling of self-worth?

options.why: A personality inventory is a questionnaire with many true-false or agree-disagree items that measures a range of traits.
Self-concept is all the thoughts and feelings a person has in answer to the question 'Who am I?'.
Self-efficacy is the belief in one's own ability to succeed at a particular task.
Correct. Self-esteem is a person's overall feeling of self-worth.

questions.explanation: Self-esteem is a person's overall feeling of self-worth.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the parenting style that sets firm rules but explains them, listens and is warm?

options.why: Correct. Authoritative parenting is the parenting style that sets firm rules but explains them, listens and is warm.
Temperament is a person's characteristic emotional reactivity and intensity, which appears early in life.
Authoritarian parenting is the parenting style that sets strict rules and expects obedience, with little warmth or discussion.
Permissive parenting is the parenting style that makes few demands and sets few limits.

questions.explanation: Authoritative parenting is the parenting style that sets firm rules but explains them, listens and is warm.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes transcranial magnetic stimulation?

options.text: The treatment in which repeated magnetic pulses are applied to the surface of the brain to treat depression
options.why: Correct. This is what transcranial magnetic stimulation means.

options.text: Any drug that acts on the brain to treat the symptoms of a psychological disorder
options.why: That describes psychotropic medication.

options.text: The treatment for severe depression in which a brief electric current is passed through the brain of an anesthetized patient
options.why: That describes electroconvulsive therapy.

options.text: The now-abandoned form of psychosurgery that cut the nerves connecting the frontal lobes to the rest of the brain
options.why: That describes a lobotomy.

questions.explanation: Transcranial magnetic stimulation is the treatment in which repeated magnetic pulses are applied to the surface of the brain to treat depression.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes aphasia?

options.text: An impairment of language caused by brain damage
options.why: Correct. This is what aphasia means.

options.text: The arrangement in which each hemisphere controls the opposite side of the body
options.why: That describes contralateral control.

options.text: The area in the left frontal lobe that controls speech production
options.why: That describes Broca's area.

options.text: The tendency for each side of the brain to handle certain functions, such as language in the left hemisphere
options.why: That describes hemispheric specialization.

questions.explanation: Aphasia is an impairment of language caused by brain damage.

questions.stem: What is the dependent variable in this study?

options.why: A hypothesis is a prediction, not a variable.

options.text: The number of other people present
options.why: This was manipulated by the researchers: it is the independent variable.
Correct. The dependent variable is the outcome that the researchers measured.

options.text: The condition to which each one was assigned
options.why: This describes the independent variable.

questions.explanation: The dependent variable is the outcome that the researchers measured.

questions.stem: Immediately after firing, a neuron cannot fire again until it has reset. What is this pause called?

options.why: Correct. The refractory period is the brief pause after a neuron fires during which it cannot fire again.
The resting potential is the stable negative charge inside a neuron when it is not firing.
The threshold is the level of stimulation that must be reached for a neuron to fire.
Reuptake is the process in which the sending neuron reabsorbs leftover neurotransmitters from the synapse.

questions.explanation: The refractory period is the brief pause after a neuron fires during which it cannot fire again.

questions.stem: Rubbing a bumped elbow reduces the pain because the touch signals close off the pain signals in the spinal cord. Which theory explains this?

options.why: Correct. The gate control theory is the theory that the spinal cord has a gate that can block pain signals or let them pass to the brain.
Phantom limb sensation is the feeling of pain or touch in a limb that has been amputated.
Kinesthesis is the sense of the position and movement of body parts, based on receptors in muscles and joints.
The vestibular sense is the sense of balance and head position, based on the semicircular canals of the inner ear.

questions.explanation: The gate control theory is the theory that the spinal cord has a gate that can block pain signals or let them pass to the brain.

questions.stem: Without evidence, Hugo is convinced that his coworkers, neighbors and friends are all plotting against him, and he has felt this way for years. Which disorder does this suggest?

options.why: Dependent personality disorder is the personality disorder marked by an excessive need to be taken care of and by clinging, submissive behavior.
Correct. Paranoid personality disorder is the personality disorder marked by lasting distrust and suspicion of others.
Borderline personality disorder is the personality disorder marked by unstable moods, relationships and self-image, and by impulsive behavior.
Histrionic personality disorder is the personality disorder marked by excessive emotion and attention seeking.

questions.explanation: Paranoid personality disorder is the personality disorder marked by lasting distrust and suspicion of others.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes lithium?

options.text: A drug that reduces hallucinations and delusions by blocking dopamine receptors
options.why: That describes an antipsychotic drug.

options.text: The mood-stabilizing drug used to treat bipolar disorder
options.why: Correct. This is what lithium means.

options.text: A drug that reduces tension by depressing central nervous system activity and can be addictive
options.why: That describes an antianxiety drug.

options.text: The involuntary movements of the face and tongue that can result from long-term use of antipsychotic drugs
options.why: That describes tardive dyskinesia.

questions.explanation: Lithium is the mood-stabilizing drug used to treat bipolar disorder.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the part of working memory that briefly holds images and spatial information?

options.why: Correct. The visuospatial sketchpad is the part of working memory that briefly holds images and spatial information.
Long-term potentiation is the strengthening of the connections between neurons after repeated activation, which is the biological basis of memory.
The central executive is the part of working memory that directs attention and coordinates the other parts.
The phonological loop is the part of working memory that briefly holds spoken and written words.

questions.explanation: The visuospatial sketchpad is the part of working memory that briefly holds images and spatial information.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes multiple intelligences?

options.text: The single underlying mental ability that Spearman believed affects performance on all mental tasks
options.why: That describes general intelligence.

options.text: The steady rise in average intelligence test scores over the generations
options.why: That describes the Flynn effect.

options.text: The theory that people have several independent kinds of intelligence, such as musical and interpersonal
options.why: Correct. This is what multiple intelligences means.

options.text: Originally, mental age divided by chronological age and multiplied by 100
options.why: That describes the intelligence quotient.

questions.explanation: Multiple intelligences is the theory that people have several independent kinds of intelligence, such as musical and interpersonal.

questions.stem: Raccoons trained to drop coins into a box began rubbing the coins together as if washing food, despite getting no reward for it. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: The law of effect is Thorndike's principle that behaviors followed by good outcomes become more likely and those followed by bad outcomes become less likely.
Correct. Instinctive drift is the tendency of a trained animal to return to its natural, inborn behaviors.
Learned helplessness is the passive giving up that follows repeated experiences of being unable to avoid bad events.
A secondary reinforcer is a reinforcer, such as money or praise, that gets its power through association with other rewards.

questions.explanation: Instinctive drift is the tendency of a trained animal to return to its natural, inborn behaviors.

questions.stem: The word 'unkindly' has three meaningful parts: un, kind and ly. Each of these parts is which of the following?

options.why: Correct. A morpheme is the smallest unit of language that carries meaning.
A phoneme is the smallest distinctive unit of sound in a language.
Semantics is the rules by which we get meaning from words and sentences.
Grammar is the whole system of rules in a language that lets people communicate.

questions.explanation: A morpheme is the smallest unit of language that carries meaning.

questions.stem: Another research team repeats this study with new subjects and obtains the same result. What is this called?

options.why: That is how subjects are placed in conditions.
Correct. Replication is repeating a study to see whether the finding holds.
That is explaining the study to participants afterward.
That is an in-depth study of one individual.

questions.explanation: Replication is repeating a study to see whether the finding holds.

questions.stem: A monitor shows a patient her muscle tension in real time, and she learns to relax her forehead muscles to prevent headaches. Which technique is this?

options.why: Aversion therapy is the behavioral treatment that pairs an unwanted behavior with an unpleasant stimulus.
A token economy is the behavioral system in which people earn tokens for desired behavior and exchange them for rewards.
Correct. Biofeedback is the technique of using electronic monitoring to show a person their body's signals so that they can learn to control them.
Applied behavior analysis is the use of the principles of conditioning to increase helpful behaviors and reduce harmful ones.

questions.explanation: Biofeedback is the technique of using electronic monitoring to show a person their body's signals so that they can learn to control them.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes random sampling?

options.text: A sample made up of whoever is easiest for the researcher to reach
options.why: That describes a convenience sample.

options.text: The selecting of participants so that every member of the population has an equal chance of being chosen
options.why: Correct. This is what random sampling means.

options.text: The extent to which the findings of a study apply to people beyond the sample
options.why: That describes generalizability.

options.text: A sample whose characteristics match those of the population it is drawn from
options.why: That describes a representative sample.

questions.explanation: Random sampling is the selecting of participants so that every member of the population has an equal chance of being chosen.

questions.stem: Another research team repeats this study with new subjects and obtains the same result. What is this called?

options.why: That is how subjects are placed in conditions.
Correct. Replication is repeating a study to see whether the finding holds.
That is an in-depth study of one individual.
That is explaining the study to participants afterward.

questions.explanation: Replication is repeating a study to see whether the finding holds.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes restoration?

options.text: The theory that dreams are the brain's attempt to make sense of random neural activity during sleep
options.why: That describes the activation-synthesis theory.

options.text: The theory that dreaming helps sort and strengthen the day's memories
options.why: That describes the consolidation theory.

options.text: The strengthening of memories that takes place during sleep
options.why: That describes memory consolidation.

options.text: The repair of body and brain tissue that takes place during sleep
options.why: Correct. This is what restoration means.

questions.explanation: Restoration is the repair of body and brain tissue that takes place during sleep.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as research that compares identical and fraternal twins to estimate the influence of heredity?

options.why: Correct. A twin study is research that compares identical and fraternal twins to estimate the influence of heredity.
Nurture is the influence of environmental factors, such as upbringing and experience, on behavior and mental processes.
Eugenics is the discredited movement that misused ideas about heredity to argue for selective breeding of humans.
The evolutionary perspective is the approach that explains behavior through natural selection of traits that helped ancestors survive and reproduce.

questions.explanation: A twin study is research that compares identical and fraternal twins to estimate the influence of heredity.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a possible third variable that could explain the correlation?

options.text: The number of hours of social media use per day
options.why: This is one of the two variables that were measured.
Correct. A third variable could influence both measures and so produce the correlation.
This is the statistic, not a variable.
This is one of the two variables that were measured.

questions.explanation: A third variable could influence both measures and so produce the correlation.

questions.stem: Before taking part, each participant was told what the study would involve and what the risks were, and then agreed to take part. Which ethical guideline does this meet?

options.why: That is a research procedure, not an ethical guideline.
Correct. Participants must agree to take part after being told what the study involves.
Debriefing happens after the study.
Confidentiality is keeping participants' data private.

questions.explanation: Participants must agree to take part after being told what the study involves.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the Big Five trait of being kind, trusting and cooperative?

options.why: Emotional stability is the Big Five trait of being calm and secure rather than anxious and moody.
Openness to experience is the Big Five trait of being imaginative, curious and willing to try new things.
Conscientiousness is the Big Five trait of being organized, careful and self-disciplined.
Correct. Agreeableness is the Big Five trait of being kind, trusting and cooperative.

questions.explanation: Agreeableness is the Big Five trait of being kind, trusting and cooperative.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as a readiness to perceive something in a particular way because of expectations?

options.why: Correct. A perceptual set is a readiness to perceive something in a particular way because of expectations.
Selective attention is the focusing of awareness on one stimulus while ignoring others.
Inattentional blindness is the failure to notice a visible object because attention is directed elsewhere.
Bottom-up processing is perception that starts with the raw sensory input and builds up to a complete picture.

questions.explanation: A perceptual set is a readiness to perceive something in a particular way because of expectations.

questions.stem: After taking a drug, a person sees vivid images that are not there and loses track of time. Which type of drug is this most likely to be?

options.why: A depressant is a drug, such as alcohol, that slows neural activity and body functions.
A stimulant is a drug, such as caffeine or cocaine, that speeds up neural activity and body functions.
An opioid is a drug, such as heroin, that relieves pain by acting on endorphin receptors and is highly addictive.
Correct. A hallucinogen is a drug, such as marijuana, that distorts perception and can cause sensory experiences without sensory input.

questions.explanation: A hallucinogen is a drug, such as marijuana, that distorts perception and can cause sensory experiences without sensory input.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the form of sensation seeking that involves a desire for risky physical activities?

options.why: Correct. Thrill and adventure seeking is the form of sensation seeking that involves a desire for risky physical activities.
Experience seeking is the form of sensation seeking that involves a desire for new experiences through travel, art and unusual lifestyles.
Boredom susceptibility is the form of sensation seeking that involves a strong dislike of repetition and routine.
Disinhibition is the form of sensation seeking that involves a loss of self-restraint, as at wild parties.

questions.explanation: Thrill and adventure seeking is the form of sensation seeking that involves a desire for risky physical activities.

questions.stem: A car crash damages a driver's spinal cord. Which part of the nervous system has been injured?

options.why: The peripheral nervous system is the sensory and motor nerves that connect the brain and spinal cord to the rest of the body.
The parasympathetic nervous system is the division of the autonomic nervous system that calms the body and conserves energy.
Correct. The central nervous system is the brain and spinal cord.
The autonomic nervous system is the division of the peripheral nervous system that controls glands and internal organs without conscious effort.

questions.explanation: The central nervous system is the brain and spinal cord.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes bipolar II disorder?

options.text: A state of extreme energy, overconfidence, racing thoughts and little need for sleep
options.why: That describes mania.

options.text: The disorder in which a person alternates between depression and a milder form of mania called hypomania
options.why: Correct. This is what bipolar II disorder means.

options.text: The disorder in which a person has full manic episodes, usually alternating with depression
options.why: That describes bipolar I disorder.

options.text: The disorder in which a person has a mildly depressed mood on most days for at least two years
options.why: That describes persistent depressive disorder.

questions.explanation: Bipolar II disorder is the disorder in which a person alternates between depression and a milder form of mania called hypomania.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the defense mechanism of turning unacceptable impulses into socially valued activities?

options.why: Repression is the defense mechanism of pushing anxiety-arousing thoughts and memories out of awareness.
Correct. Sublimation is the defense mechanism of turning unacceptable impulses into socially valued activities.
Reaction formation is the defense mechanism of acting in the opposite way to one's unacceptable impulses.
Regression is the defense mechanism of retreating to behavior from an earlier stage of development.

questions.explanation: Sublimation is the defense mechanism of turning unacceptable impulses into socially valued activities.

questions.stem: A patient stands rigid in one position for several hours and does not respond to anyone. Which symptom is this?

options.why: A delusion is a false belief, often of persecution or grandeur, that a person holds despite clear evidence against it.
Correct. Catatonia is a disturbance of movement in which a person may remain motionless for hours or move without purpose.
A hallucination is a sensory experience, such as hearing voices, that occurs without any outside stimulus.
Disorganized speech is the jumbled, illogical speech, sometimes called word salad, that is a symptom of schizophrenia.

questions.explanation: Catatonia is a disturbance of movement in which a person may remain motionless for hours or move without purpose.

questions.stem: Without considering any alternatives, Ravi plans to join the family business because his parents always expected it. Which identity status is this?

options.why: Identity moratorium is the identity status of a person who is actively exploring options but has not yet made a commitment.
Correct. Identity foreclosure is the identity status of a person who has made a commitment without exploring options.
Identity achievement is the identity status of a person who has explored options and made a commitment.
Identity diffusion is the identity status of a person who has neither explored options nor made a commitment.

questions.explanation: Identity foreclosure is the identity status of a person who has made a commitment without exploring options.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes an agonist?

options.text: The need for larger doses of a drug to get the same effect after repeated use
options.why: That describes tolerance.

options.text: A drug that decreases the action of a neurotransmitter, for example by blocking its receptors
options.why: That describes an antagonist.

options.text: The unpleasant physical and psychological symptoms that follow stopping an addictive drug
options.why: That describes withdrawal.

options.text: A drug that increases the action of a neurotransmitter, for example by mimicking it
options.why: Correct. This is what an agonist means.

questions.explanation: An agonist is a drug that increases the action of a neurotransmitter, for example by mimicking it.

questions.stem: Another research team repeats this study with new subjects and obtains the same result. What is this called?

options.why: That is an in-depth study of one individual.
That is explaining the study to participants afterward.
Correct. Replication is repeating a study to see whether the finding holds.
That is how subjects are placed in conditions.

questions.explanation: Replication is repeating a study to see whether the finding holds.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes an optimistic explanatory style?

options.text: The tendency to explain our own behavior by the situation but other people's behavior by their traits
options.why: That describes the actor-observer bias.

options.text: The habit of explaining bad events as lasting, affecting everything and caused by oneself
options.why: That describes a pessimistic explanatory style.

options.text: The feeling of being worse off than the people one compares oneself with
options.why: That describes relative deprivation.

options.text: The habit of explaining bad events as temporary, specific and caused by outside factors
options.why: Correct. This is what an optimistic explanatory style means.

questions.explanation: An optimistic explanatory style is the habit of explaining bad events as temporary, specific and caused by outside factors.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes stability and change?

options.text: The view that development happens in distinct stages, like a staircase
options.why: That describes discontinuous development.

options.text: The developmental question of how heredity and experience together shape a person
options.why: That describes nature and nurture.

options.text: Research that compares people of different ages at one point in time
options.why: That describes a cross-sectional study.

options.text: The developmental question of which traits stay the same through life and which ones alter
options.why: Correct. This is what stability and change means.

questions.explanation: Stability and change is the developmental question of which traits stay the same through life and which ones alter.

questions.stem: Which of the following would be a confounding variable in this study?

options.text: Each one was assigned to a condition at random
options.why: Random assignment reduces confounding; it is not a confound.

options.text: The two groups differed in amusement at the end of the study
options.why: That is the dependent variable, the result being measured.

options.text: The group holding the pen between the teeth saw the cartoons in color, and the other group saw them in black and white
options.why: Correct. It differs between the groups along with the independent variable, so it could explain the results instead.

options.text: One group differed from the other in the facial expression produced by holding a pen
options.why: That is the independent variable itself.

questions.explanation: It differs between the groups along with the independent variable, so it could explain the results instead.

questions.stem: Scores on a test are normally distributed with a mean of 100 and a standard deviation of 15. About what percentage of scores are above 100?

options.why: This does not match the 68–95 rule for a normal distribution.
This does not match the 68–95 rule for a normal distribution.
Correct. A normal distribution is symmetrical, so half the scores lie above the mean.
This does not match the 68–95 rule for a normal distribution.

questions.explanation: A normal distribution is symmetrical, so half the scores lie above the mean. (85 and 115 are one standard deviation from the mean; 70 and 130 are two.)

questions.title: Article analysis: a study of attention to the road

parts.prompt: Identify the research method used in the study.

rubric.criterion: Identifies the method as an experiment.
rubric.example: The study is an experiment: the researchers manipulated a variable and randomly assigned the subjects to conditions.

parts.prompt: State the operational definition of attention to the road.

rubric.criterion: States how the variable was measured in this study.
rubric.example: Attention to the road was defined as the number of road signs out of 30 that each participant failed to notice.

parts.prompt: Describe the meaning of the difference between the two group averages.

rubric.criterion: Accurately describes which group scored higher or lower and what that means for the variable measured.
rubric.example: The phone group missed more road signs. On average, the value was 11.4 for the group that talked on the phone and 4.9 for the group that drove without a phone, and a p value of 0.01 means a difference this large is unlikely to be due to chance.

parts.prompt: Identify at least one ethical guideline applied by the researchers.

rubric.criterion: Identifies an ethical guideline that the summary shows was followed.
rubric.example: Informed consent: participants agreed to take part after being told about the study. (Also acceptable: debriefing; the right to withdraw; approval by an institutional review board.)

parts.prompt: Explain the extent to which the research findings may or may not be generalizable, using specific and relevant evidence from the study.

rubric.criterion: Explains a limit (or strength) of generalizability with reference to the sample.
rubric.example: The sample was 64 licensed drivers from one city, so the findings may not apply to people of other ages, cultures or backgrounds. Because the sample was not randomly selected from a wider population, it may not be representative.

parts.prompt: Explain how at least one of the research findings supports or refutes the researchers' hypothesis.

rubric.criterion: Uses a specific finding from the study as evidence.
rubric.example: The phone group missed more road signs. (11.4 compared with 4.9).

rubric.criterion: Explains how the finding supports the hypothesis, using a psychological concept.
rubric.example: This supports the hypothesis that phone use affects attention to the road. Because subjects were randomly assigned, the difference can be attributed to phone use. The finding illustrates selective attention and inattentional blindness: attention is limited, so people fail to notice visible objects when attention is elsewhere.

questions.title: Evidence-based question: Does sleep improve memory?

parts.prompt: Propose a specific and defensible claim, based in psychological science, that responds to the question.

rubric.criterion: States a claim that answers the question and can be supported by the sources.
rubric.example: Sleep improves memory because memories are consolidated during sleep.

parts.prompt: (i) Support your claim using at least one piece of specific and relevant evidence from one of the sources. (ii) Explain how the evidence supports your claim, using a psychological perspective, theory, concept or research finding learned in AP Psychology.

rubric.criterion: Uses specific, relevant evidence from one source and names the source.
rubric.example: In Source A, students who slept recalled a mean of 31 of 40 word pairs, compared with 22 for students who stayed awake.

rubric.criterion: Explains how the evidence supports the claim.
rubric.example: This supports the claim through memory consolidation: during sleep, the hippocampus and cortex strengthen newly encoded memories, so the sleep group stored the word pairs better. Because the study was an experiment with random assignment, sleep can be said to have caused the difference.

rubric.criterion: Correctly applies a psychological concept in the explanation.
rubric.example: The concept must be named and applied correctly, as in the model explanation.

parts.prompt: (i) Support your claim using an additional piece of specific and relevant evidence from a different source. (ii) Explain how this evidence supports your claim, using a different psychological perspective, theory, concept or research finding.

rubric.criterion: Uses specific, relevant evidence from a different source and names the source.
rubric.example: In Source B, participants who had more slow-wave sleep completed the maze faster the next morning (r = +0.55).

rubric.criterion: Explains how the evidence supports the claim.
rubric.example: This supports the claim because NREM stage 3 sleep is linked to strengthening the neural connections formed during learning (long-term potentiation), so more deep sleep goes with better retention of the maze.

rubric.criterion: Correctly applies a different psychological concept from the one used in part B.
rubric.example: The concept must differ from the one used in part B and be applied correctly.
